review_notes: Read the whole target file (all 426 lines) and checked every public declaration against the underlying definitions in the same development: `CKN.IsWeakDivFreeL2` and `WeakTestFunction` (`LeanPool/CaffarelliKohnNirenberg/Leray/JSpace.lean`, lines 35–40; `LeanPool/CaffarelliKohnNirenberg/Foundation/Sobolev/TestFunction.lean`, lines 24–40), the Fourier symbols and physical operators `lerayApplyFormula`, `lerayFourierMultiplier`, `lerayProjectionL2`, `stokesFourierMultiplier`, `stokesL2Operator` plus their divergence-free a.e. lemmas (`LeanPool/CaffarelliKohnNirenberg/Leray/FourierLeray.lean`, lines 52–54, 191–253, 544–657), the realification maps `complexifyVectorL2`, `realPartVectorL2`, `realLerayProjection`, `realStokesOperator` (`LeanPool/CaffarelliKohnNirenberg/Leray/FourierRealification.lean`, lines 101–127, 199–227), and a consumer that applies the general theorem (`LeanPool/CaffarelliKohnNirenberg/Leray/FourierHeatDivergence.lean`, lines 67–88). Non-vacuity checks: (a) the test-function predicate is nonempty (constant-0 and any bump function) and materially constraining — it is equivalent to the closure description of `J` (`LeanPool/CaffarelliKohnNirenberg/Leray/JSpaceFourierLimit.lean`, line 231: `isInJ_iff_weakDivFree`); (b) the hypothesis `hv` of `realPart_isWeakDivFree_of_fourierOrthogonal` is satisfiable in general (e.g. any nonzero field whose Fourier transform is pointwise orthogonal to `complexifyFrequency`) and is concretely discharged for the Leray and Stokes ranges via `lerayFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae` and `stokesFourierMultiplier_divergence_free_ae`, so the specialized theorems are not instances of an unsatisfiable hypothesis; (c) the conventions line up: `weakTestGradientSchwartz_apply` shows the encoded field really has components `ψ.partialDeriv i`, and the `2 * Real.pi * Complex.I` factor together with `complexifyFrequency` is the correct derivative symbol, so the orthogonality hypothesis is exactly the vanishing of the divergence coefficient, not an unrelated statement; (d) `0 < t` in the Stokes results is genuinely required by `stokesFourierMultiplier`/`stokesL2Operator` (the bound `1/√(2 e t)`), and the real part of the heat-regularized Leray–Stokes multiplier applied to a conjugate-symmetric (real-data) Fourier field is not identically zero, so `realStokesOperator` is not the zero operator and the divergence-free claims are substantive rather than tautological; (e) the bridging lemma `realPartVectorL2Representative_eq_ae` is not definitional (`realPartVectorL2` is an `Lp` map whose coercion is only a.e. equal to pointwise `realPartValue`), so the two Leray/Stokes conclusions are not trivially restatements. I did not find a declaration whose assumptions are inconsistent, whose domain is unintentionally empty, whose claim is trivialized, or which omits a needed conclusion relative to its stated purpose. Limitation: nothing could be compiled or executed, so this judgment rests on reading; the constant-2 bound in `gradientOfCovectorLinear_norm_bound` is non-sharp but valid and lies outside this rubric.
